1 Statement and preliminaries
A complete deterministic automaton is a triple(Q, Σ,δ) with finite state setQ and total transition functionδ:
Q×Σ→Q. We use right actions:qw =δ(q,w ) andSw ={qw :q∈S}. Length counts letters ofΣ. The automaton
is strongly connected if every state reaches every other state, and synchronizing if|Qw|= 1 for some wordw. A
subset S is a reachable image ifS =Qv for a wordv, possibly empty. Put
ac(S,A ) = min{|w|:A ⊈Sw or|Sw|<|S|}, ∅̸=A ⊊S⊆Q.
Here avoidance means omitting at least one state ofA, not all ofA. Call a word safe ifA⊆Sw and|Sw|=|S|.
The upper boundn−|A|is due to Szykuła [1, Lemma 2]; it is restated as Lemma 3 in his 2026 survey [2].
Open Problem 4 asks for tight bounds depending on both cardinalities. Figure 2 of that survey already gives
the case (|S|,|A|) = (2, 1). Ferens, Szykuła and Vorel [3, p. 46:6] also discuss sharpness for a related fixed-state
avoiding-or-compressing alternative. We make no priority claim for these earlier cases. Here we give explicit
cardinality-dependent witnesses with all the structural requirements imposed simultaneously.

Theorem 1. The following bounds hold, and every lower bound has a binary witness.
1. F(n,r + 1,r ) =n−r for n≥2 and 1≤r≤n−1.
2. F(n,r + 2,r ) =n−r for n≥4 and 1≤r≤n−3.
3. For r≥1, s−r≥3 and n≥2s−r−1, one has
F(n,s,r ) =n−r.
For 1≤r<n , one has F(n,n,r ) = 1.

with s−r≥3, the bound is sharp at everyn≥2s−r−1, in particular atn =r +k(s−r−1) + 2for k≥2.
